items.title: Written Test (50-75% of grade)
items.text:
I. Historical perspective of the electricity discoveries made by 1. Ampere 2. Coulomb 3. Kirchhoff 4. Volta 5. Ohm 6. Hertz 7. Boule

II. Properties of clectric charges/fields 1. sources/hazards of static electricity 2. Coulomb's Law Characteristics

III. Characteristics, sources uses, and hazards of 1. direct current(DC) 2. alternating current (AC)

IV. Concepts calculations and units of 1. current 2. voltage 3. resistance 4. power 5. energy

V. Calculations, constructions, and configuratons of CC circuits and individual components 1. series and parallel circuits 2. open and short circuits 3. Ohm’s Law 4. circuit schematics

VI. Fundamental electrical characteristics of: 1. silicon PN junctions 2. uses of single-junction devices (e.g., diodes, LEDs)

VII-B. Electrical contro! devices (Div. B) 1. switches 2. relays 3. fuses 4. ground fault circuit interrupters, and breakers

VII-C. Circuit Analysis 1. Kirchoff's Voltage Law 2. Kirchoff's Current Law

VIII. Digital Logic (25-50% of grade) 1. Digital logic gates 2. truth tables 3. universal gate sets 4. boolean expressions 5. combinational logic circuits, such as 5a. multiplexers 5b. adders

VIII. (States/Nationals only) 1. Circuit analysis using Kirchhot!’s Voltage & Current Laws

IX. Mathematical Content 1. Functions, algebraic manipulations, and systems of no more than two equations 2. 2D geometry required for interpreting vector directionality, including 2a. points 2b. parallel and perpendicular lines 2c. angles in degrees 3. Binary arithmetic 3a. Representation of whole, positive integers 3b. Addition of binary numbers 4. Logical operations as boolean expressions, including 4a. De Morgan's Law 4b. Truth Tables

items.title: Hands-On Tasks
items.text:
Participants may ask event supervisors for details of the internal wiring of any breadboards tasks.

The hands-on tasks, of stations, may include but are not limited to:

  1. Determine the value of a mystery resistor in a circuit using only voltage measurements

  2. Calculate the power supplied to a circuit.

  3. Given some wires, batteries, resistors; and 2 LEDs, hook them up so the LEDs are equally bright.

  4. Given a USB charger, read the label and provide: 4a. details of the various output power levels it can provide 4b. calculate how long tt would take to charge a specific battery

  5. Construct a logic circuit to mimic a given truth table.

  6. Troubleshoot a faulty circuit.

  7. Wire a 3-way switch using SPDT switches.

  8. Create a specified equivalent resistance from given individual resistors.

items.title: References/Tutorials
items.text:
• OpenStax, Chapters 18-23. Problems will be assigned from here.

  • UTA: Electromagnetism and Optics has many worked examples.

  • Oxford University Chemistry: Electtostatics has many problems with answers.

  • Oxford University Chemistry: Magnetism also has many problems and answers.

  • Hyperphysics offers short explanations of a wide range of topics in Electricity and Magnetism.

  • [A one-page tutorial on Electricity, Magnetism, & Electromagnetism](https://www.sciencebuddies.org/science-fair-projects/references/electricity-magnetism-electromagnetism-tutorial

  • Electreonics Notes offers great videos describing a wide variety of circuits.

  • Zak's Lab Physics offers great videos as well as Test questions.
